title: Analyzing Engram Reactivation and Long-Range Connectivity
author: Refaeli, Kreisel, et al.

steps.title: PBS Washes to Remove Cryoprotectant
steps.instruction: Remove residual cryoprotectant by washing slices in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Transfer slices from cryoprotectant to PBS and shake for 15 min.
Replace PBS twice, shaking 15 min each wash.

steps.title: Block Tissue and Prepare Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Block non‑specific binding and ready the primary antibody solution.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slices in blocking solution while shaking at 70 rpm for 1 h at ~25 °C.
Prepare primary antibody solution.

steps.title: Incubate Slices with Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Stain slices with c‑Fos primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slices in primary antibody solution, shaking mildly at 4 °C for 7 days.

steps.title: Post‑Primary PBS Washes
steps.instruction: Remove unbound primary antibody with PBS washes.

substeps.instruction: Wash slices in PBS, shaking 15 min.
Perform a second PBS wash, shaking 15 min.
Incubate slices in secondary antibody (AF 647) solution, shaking at 70 rpm for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash slices in PBS for 15 min.
Incubate slices in DAPI (1:50,000) solution for 5 min.

steps.title: Mount Slices on Slides
steps.instruction: Place stained slices onto microscope slides.

substeps.instruction: Place slices onto microscope slides.
Allow slices to dry on slide for 20 min.
Add 1–2 drops mounting medium and seal with a coverslip.

steps.title: Place Sample on Slide
steps.instruction: Position tissue on a slide with adequate margins.

substeps.instruction: Place tissue sample on a slide, leaving sufficient space between tissue edges and slide borders.

steps.title: Create Hot‑Glue Walls with Gap
steps.instruction: Build a chamber around the tissue using hot glue, leaving a small gap.

substeps.instruction: Using a hot‑glue gun, build walls up to near tissue height, leaving a 4–5 mm gap and not sealing walls completely.

steps.title: Apply CSRC Drops to Prevent Bubbles
steps.instruction: Add clearing solution to avoid bubble formation.

substeps.instruction: Apply 1–2 drops of CSRC onto tissue to avoid bubble formation.

steps.title: Add Final Wall Layer to Tissue Height
steps.instruction: Complete the chamber walls to match tissue height.

substeps.instruction: Add the final layer of hot‑glue walls, matching tissue height.

steps.title: Seal Slide with Coverslip (Add Extra Glue if Needed)
steps.instruction: Close the chamber and optionally reinforce for immersion objectives.

substeps.instruction: Before glue sets, seal the slide top with a coverslip, ensuring even contact and no holes.
If using an immersion objective, apply an additional hot‑glue layer above the coverslip.

steps.title: Fill Chamber with CSRC
steps.instruction: Introduce clearing solution into the chamber.

substeps.instruction: Fill the chamber through the gap with CSRC solution.

steps.title: Seal Gap with Hot Glue
steps.instruction: Close the chamber completely, eliminating bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Seal the gap with hot glue, ensuring no bubbles remain.

description: Before initiating the following protocol, it is essential that the lab gains access to specific requirements, including genetic manipulation, immunostaining, tissue clearing, and commercialized software. Here are the key elements needed.1.Genetic manipulation: Involves using TG mice (for example, Ai14 reporter mice2) and viral vectors (for example, AAV5-c-Fos::creER), as described in the protocol.2.Immunostaining: Primary antibody (rabbit anti c-Fos, Synaptic System #226008) and secondary antibody (donkey anti rabbit, AF 647 #711-605-152, Jackson laboratory).3.The CLARITY tissue clearing technique requires multiple premade ingredients. Carefully read the protocol and tables appended to it before you begin. Details can be found in the following papers.1,3
